так згоден прийнято на додаток попрощу зазирнути чи є сенс та підсилення в циз наративах та візуалізаціях:

Cost of inaction.

What ISRM continues to absorb without this infrastructure.

Without this infrastructure, ISRM continues to absorb measurable costs across three vectors. Manual research at current volume consumes an estimated 40+ staff hours per strategic enquiry across chapter teams and central coordination. The miss rate on blind introductions — contacts approached without verified context — is approximately 30–40%, exposing the association to reputational damage on each failed or inappropriate contact. Over an 18-month horizon, the cumulative cost — staff time, missed mandate opportunities, and one reputational incident of moderate severity — is conservatively estimated at £180,000–£280,000.

The cost is not hypothetical. ISRM is already paying it: in chapter time absorbed by manual lookup, in mandate opportunities deferred or lost because a relevant expert could not be located in time, and in the latent reputational risk of every unverified introduction made under deadline pressure. This proposal does not create a new cost line. It redirects an existing cost — currently absorbed silently — into an asset that compounds.

Assumptions

  • 40 hours/enquiry: based on chapter self-reporting at comparable associations, conservative midpoint.
  • 30–40% miss rate: industry benchmark for unverified expert search in crisis response contexts.
  • £180k–£280k over 18 months: 40h × ~£50/h blended + 2–3 lost mandates at £15–25k each + 1 reputational incident remediation cost.
  • Figures are indicative, not contractual. A formal baseline measurement is part of Stage 1 discovery.

Out of scope — explicitly excluded from this proposal.

Items listed here are not unquoted future work. They are intentionally excluded.

The following items are explicitly excluded from Stage 1 scope. Each can be added as a separate Stage 2 or Stage 3 engagement with separate pricing, separate acceptance criteria, and a separate decision. Clarity here protects both parties: ISRM knows what it is buying, and the vendor knows what it is delivering. Items are listed with their exclusion rationale, not as a sales list.

  • Real-time LinkedIn data sync — mocked in prototype. Production integration scheduled for Stage 2. Rationale: OAuth integration requires LinkedIn API review cycle (4–8 weeks) outside Stage 1 timeline.
  • Stripe payment automation — manual invoicing in Stage 1. Rationale: payment flow stabilisation belongs in Stage 2 once core workflow is proven.
  • OpenSanctions real-time scoring — manual compliance check in Stage 1. Rationale: API integration is technically straightforward but adds external dependency risk before core is stabilised.
  • GDELT and World Monitor incident feeds — not included. Rationale: situational awareness module is a Stage 3 concern, predicated on Stage 2 graph engine.
  • Custom LLM training on member expertise — explicitly Stage 3. Rationale: requires Stage 2 verified corpus scale (500+ profiles) to produce training data of sufficient quality.
  • Mobile application (iOS/Android) — not included. Rationale: responsive web covers core access; native mobile is a separate product decision.
  • Multi-language UI beyond English — not included. Rationale: i18n framework is in code architecture; translation is a content cost, not a development cost, and belongs in Stage 2.
  • Chapter-specific customisations — not included. Rationale: Stage 1 delivers the platform; chapter configuration is a Stage 2 governance decision.
  • Data migration from existing CRM — not included. Rationale: seed corpus (178 profiled) is already in the new data model. Legacy CRM migration is a separate data engineering engagement.
  • Ongoing managed service beyond warranty period — not included. Rationale: warranty covers 30 days post go-live; managed service is a separate retainer arrangement, not a Stage 1 deliverable.

Any item not listed above and not in the in-scope section should be assumed out of scope. If unclear, raise in discovery call before contract signature. Items added post-signature follow the Change Request Policy below.

Cap on hours — maximum effort per module.

Hours cap protects ISRM from open-ended billing.

Each module has a maximum effort cap. If a cap is approached at 80%, the vendor escalates in writing to ISRM with options: extend the cap by written agreement at the standard hourly rate, descope the module, or defer remaining work to Stage 2. Hours above cap without written authorisation are absorbed by the vendor at no cost to ISRM. The cap is a financial discipline, not a quality compromise — quality is governed by acceptance criteria, not by hours.

Module Maximum hours At 80% (escalation trigger) Above cap (without authorisation)
Core application (Identity Vault, Consent, Audit Log, Graph Engine, Shortlist, Gap Analysis) 320 256h — escalation in writing Absorbed by vendor
Workflow package — Membership & client enquiries (per package) 80 64h — escalation in writing Absorbed by vendor
Workflow package — Developing professional expertise (per package) 80 64h — escalation in writing Absorbed by vendor
Workflow package — Situational awareness & briefings (per package) 80 64h — escalation in writing Absorbed by vendor
Integration (Stage 1: LinkedIn OAuth only) 40 32h — escalation in writing Absorbed by vendor
Total Stage 1 cap (core + all packages + integration) 520 416h — full review trigger —

Why caps matter

  • For ISRM: budget ceiling is fixed; no open-ended billing exposure.
  • For vendor: discipline to escalate early rather than absorb silently; protects margin via early conversation.
  • For both: either party can trigger the cap conversation at 80%; it is not a vendor-only obligation.

What caps do not cover

  • Hours incurred due to ISRM-initiated changes (governed by Change Request Policy).
  • Hours incurred due to third-party integration failures outside vendor control.
  • Hours incurred due to ISRM data quality issues discovered mid-engagement.
  • Hours incurred due to delay in ISRM-named-authority response beyond 5 business days.

Warranty and acceptance criteria.

Working software with measurable acceptance, not a date-based launch.

Warranty period

The warranty period is 30 calendar days post go-live. During this period, the vendor provides bug fixes at no additional cost to ISRM. The warranty does not cover: third-party integration failures outside vendor control, changes to ISRM data initiated by ISRM, or configuration changes initiated by ISRM post go-live.

Severity Definition Response time Resolution target
Critical Core workflow blocked; no workaround 4 business hours 24 hours
Major Workflow degraded; workaround exists 1 business day 72 hours
Minor Cosmetic or non-blocking 3 business days Next sprint or backlog

Acceptance criteria (checklist)

Acceptance is governed by a checklist, not by a date. The vendor delivers against each criterion; ISRM verifies. Acceptance is written confirmation from the ISRM-named authority that all criteria are met.

  1. 50 verified profiles operational in the production graph, with auditable verification trail for each.
  2. 10 sample queries processed end-to-end: search → shortlist → consent request → audit log entry → encrypted PDF export. Each query documented with timestamp and verifier signature.
  3. Audit log passes ISRM-appointed reviewer inspection: every access to a sensitive dossier has a corresponding log entry with timestamp, requester identity, consent reference, and purpose.
  4. Consent flow tested with 3 named members: each member has completed at least one disclosure approval and one disclosure rejection; both paths produce correct log entries and correct dossier visibility changes.
  5. Configurator generates tokenised proposal for 3 sample configurations: ISRM Board preset, Corporate client preset, Member preset. Each produces a unique proposal URL with the correct scope, price, and out-of-scope blocks.
  6. Warranty period completed without a critical incident un-resolved within SLA. Two or more unresolved critical incidents extend the warranty period at vendor cost until 30 consecutive critical-incident-free days are achieved.

Acceptance process

  1. ISRM has 10 business days post go-live to evaluate against the checklist above.
  2. Acceptance is provided in writing by the ISRM-named authority.
  3. If criteria are not met, the vendor corrects at no additional cost until met.
  4. If criteria remain unmet after 30 calendar days of correction effort, ISRM may invoke contract termination terms per the contract's termination clause.
  5. Payment milestones (50% initial deployment, 20% operational refinement) release only on written acceptance of the corresponding criteria.
